rationale_bullets: Dampier (83.1/391) returns off B12 Newcomer of the Year: 2,490 at 64% with a 24-5 TD-INT plus 835 rush yards as the team's #2 rusher - 'the most elusive pocket scrambler in America' (P6) - having improved accuracy and turnovers in the P4 step-up.
Ficklin (90.5/44) is the explicit tag-team piece: 10 rush TD at 8.4 per carry, a start, 3-0 passing - 'these two don't mind sharing' and could share the field.

The subtraction is the OC: Beck (the '25 fix) followed Whittingham to Michigan; McGiven ran the 'similar' QB-as-#1-rusher offense at Utah State with more vertical shots - continuity is partial, not full.
70 = clearly above average: the best returning dual-threat tape in the league, tempered by the scheme handoff and Dampier's injury history.
Parker (81.4) returns as the bellcow: 981 at 6.6 - the #2 per-carry mark in P4 (min. 100 carries) behind only the Heisman runner-up.
Depth is real: Bray (67.7; 272 at 6.8 true-FR speed), Chavez-Soto (81.4 at SJSU; the 'short-yardage bulldozer'), 5* FR Bell (PS#28).
The caveat: the school-record 3,462 rush yards came behind the #2 Run Push line in the country - which is entirely gone. 65 = solidly above average on the back's own tape.
The top three pass-catchers left: Davis (75.3; 725), drafted TE Bentley (76.9; 620), Buchanan (427 at 16.4) to Michigan.

The imports are targeted: Pegan (73.7; 929 at 15.4 - WITH new OC McGiven at Utah State, All-MW, 4* transfer grade) + Shoels (63.9; 768, All-MW, 4* grade); returners Simmons (66.8; 280 at 18.7), N.Johnson (73.8), Whittemore, and TE Andrews off the injury year fill in.
Scalley's superlative ('best WR crew we've ever had at Utah' / PS: 'most dangerous in his 20 years') runs against a 13-years-without-a-1,000-yarder history and MW-graded tape.
52 = average-plus: real additions with scheme fit, unproven vs P4 coverage.
grades_detail.g5_guard_note: Pegan/Shoels are MW-graded 4*-transfers; the McGiven connection is the offset that holds 52

rationale_bullets: All five starters from the 'best line ever' (94th-pctile pass-block, #2 Run Push, 266 rush at 6.0, 14 sacks) are gone - Fano (83.9/822) and Lomu (68.4/823) as FIRST-ROUND early declares - plus ace line coach Harding.

What returns is the jumbo package: Moea'i (62.2/336) and Olson (64.6/295) step in at guard, Harrison (68.2/143; yr-4 bonus season) battles Kema (Ohio State) at center, Williams (60.7/156; yr-4 override, LT1 on both May prints).
The upside pieces are unproven here: Jefferson (Montana State FCS champ) at RT and 5* FR Obot (PS#9, 'could start right away' - PS starts him at LG).
The Utah OL pipeline ('next in a long line of elite Ute blockers') is a real prior, but 'the biggest question mark on offense' (PS) is the sober read. 46 = fringe-below-average with a high ceiling.
grades_detail.g5_guard_note: Jefferson FCS-graded; Obot has zero college tape - pipeline prior is the only lift

rationale_bullets: Both starting DEs and the top three DTs are gone: Daley (92.0/513; led P4 in sacks/game) and Lea'ea to Michigan, L.Fano (78.8/515) as an NFL early declare, Vimahi expired, Vakalahi to Penn State.

And the '25 unit was already the problem: 181 rush ypg allowed at 4.8 - Utah's worst since 1996 - with RDEF 43rd/TACK 18th pctile ('the worst in the Big 12 against the run… that's not them' - Athlon scouting quote).

The reload: Holtzclaw (73.8/341 - best returning tape) and Dillon (61.9/341; PS: 35 tkl, 3.5 sk) move up; Moe (83.1/213 SJSU) is premium small-sample; Day (75.4/654; 14 NT starts) is the volume add; Kaufusi/Sepulona inside.
PS: 'As the DL goes, so goes the entire defense this season.' 44 = below average until proven.
grades_detail.g5_guard_note: Moe/Day/Samsula tape is MW/CUSA-graded; guard holds the unit at 44

rationale_bullets: Hall (70.1/642; #1 tackler, 13 st, 67 tkl) returns as the anchor of what was PS's #12 corps.

Everything else thinned: Barton (61.7/637), Damuni (78.7/313), and nickel Snowden (69.3/632, to Michigan) are gone, and the staff signed NO transfers - Polu (68.6/96), Reynolds (65.2/239; PS starter line 4 st, 28 tkl), Elliss (68.0/114) inherit roles.
PS's own read: 'less experienced and talented.' 46 = fringe-below-average: one proven starter plus projection.
The safety room is the strength: Bennee (74.1/676; 4 INT, 9 pd - 'a play-maker' with All-B12 hype), plus Evans (yr-4 medical return, on all three May prints) and 6th-year Ritchie back from injuries.

The corner room turned over: Snowden (Michigan) and four others left for P4 rosters; E.Davis ('Scooby'; 58.2/627, 20 starts over two years) is the lone returning corner, with Reed (77.3/580 at Akron - genuine tape; PS: 18 st, 79 tkl L2Y) vs Chenault (66.2/434 USF) for the other spot and JUCO Caldwell (82.7/106) at nickel.
The lineage is elite: PDR #3 then #2 the last two years, a 22-year pick-six streak - 'they lose two starters but remain one of the nation's best (as always)' (PS).
58 = above average: proven safeties + real corner tape additions, thinner margins than the Utah standard.

Everyone returns from the 81st-pctile unit (PS #29 STR): K Curtis ('Legatron,' 60+ leg: 10-14 with a 54-long, 60 TB on 83 KO), P Phillips (42.3-42.9 avg, ~40 net), PR Carvalho (75-yd PR TD), KR Whittemore.
PS: 'with everyone back will move up even more this year.'
62 = solidly above average: proven legs and return game; Curtis's FG volume (14-15 attempts) is the only sample caveat.
